Field note 04 / United States benchmark

A U.S. ecosystem built around shared capacity.

26 October 2026Public sourcesUS benchmark

A narrow benchmark on the public layers that connect research access, interoperable systems and safer deployment.

By Superintelligence SG · Published 26 October 2026 · Version 1.0
Editorial analysis of public sources. Observations and interpretation are presented separately.

View sources

The question

What public structures make a national AI ecosystem more than a collection of companies, models and investment announcements?

Capacity needs a public layer.

The U.S. record points to two distinct layers: shared infrastructure that makes computing, data, models and technical help reachable by more researchers; and standards work that makes agent systems easier to connect and secure. Neither layer proves adoption, safety or benefit in any specific deployment. Together, they make those outcomes more possible to study.

What we observed.

On 1 September 2026, the U.S. National Science Foundation announced the National AI Research Resource Operations Center. NSF describes it as the operational backbone for a national portal and coordinated resources across computing, data, models, tools, training and support.

On 17 February 2026, NIST's Center for AI Standards and Innovation announced an AI Agent Standards Initiative focused on interoperable and secure agent systems. Its stated work includes industry standards, open-source protocols, and research on agent security and identity.

Two public signals.

They describe capability and standards infrastructure, not a ranking of the U.S. AI ecosystem or an evaluation of individual organisations.

01 / Access

NAIRR is being operationalised as shared research capacity.

NSF says the NAIRR Operations Center will coordinate participating resource providers, integrate computing, data, models and tools, operate a national portal, and support users through technical help and training. The announcement says the earlier pilot supported more than 800 research projects and thousands of innovators and students nationwide.

Read NSF's NAIRR Operations Center announcement ↗

Why it mattersShared access can widen who can test ideas and produce evidence. It does not tell us which research outcomes will translate into durable public or commercial value.

02 / Interoperability

Agent systems are being treated as a standards and security problem.

NIST says its AI Agent Standards Initiative will convene work around industry-led standards, community-led open-source protocols, and research on agent security and identity. The announcement frames interoperability and security as conditions for a developing agent ecosystem.

Read NIST's AI Agent Standards Initiative announcement ↗

Why it mattersStandards can make systems easier to connect, inspect and govern. An announced initiative is not evidence that a standard is adopted or that a particular agent is safe.

What this benchmark leaves out.

These official announcements do not provide a census of the U.S. AI ecosystem, a measure of regional access, or comparable evidence about deployment outcomes. They also do not establish the performance or safety of any individual model, vendor or application. This note is a starting point for comparison, not a global directory.

Keep Singapore at the centre.
